sections.title: Identification and form
sections.text: The catalogue entry represents Olea europaea, the olive, rather than the whole genus. This evergreen tree or large shrub can reach about 10 m; it is native to the Mediterranean region and widely cultivated.

sections.title: Leaves, flowers and fruit
sections.text: The opposite, leathery evergreen leaves are about 3–6 cm long and silvery beneath. The white flowers, 4–7 mm across, grow in small clusters. The drupe is about 1.5–3 cm long.

sections.title: Food uses
sections.text: The fruits are eaten as olives after processing and are used to produce olive oil. They are rarely eaten fresh because of their bitterness.
